briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Clears Out Bad Actors While D.C. Clears a Path for Psychedelics
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales and operators are still finding room to expand and win fights with regulators — even as the state makes an example of a noncompliant vape brand and a GOP gubernatorial hopeful courts industry cash with a wholesale-tax repeal pledge. Nationally, momentum keeps building: the FDA is publicly workshopping a psilocybin approval pathway, Compass Pathways' psilocybin just cleared a six-month durability bar, and MSOs are striking bigger, bolder deals as rescheduling grinds forward.

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion since launch — August alone generated about $259 million, pushing cumulative adult-use sales above $15.41 billion and medical sales above $1.63 billion.

$4M dispensary-restaurant hybrid set to open this fall in Muskegon — the winery-style concept tests whether an elevated cannabis experience can support higher price points in one of the state's earliest adult-use markets.

Jars Cannabis forces removal of a police surveillance camera — the 54-store chain reached a deal with Madison Heights to take down a Flock camera aimed at its parking lot entrance since a 2022 licensing settlement.
Governor candidate John James pledges to repeal the 24% wholesale tax — Michigan cannabis executives have already written the GOP congressman about $90,000 in checks to back his run.

Muha Meds maker hit with record $2M fine and shutdown — the CRA revoked Michigan Investments 10's processor licenses over 'egregious violations,' including an extraction-room camera pointed at a wall instead of the activity it was supposed to monitor.

national.text: FDA hearing puts psilocybin and methylone on an approval path — officials gathered expert input on the therapeutic potential of psychedelic drugs for serious mental health conditions at a White Oak hearing.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin clears a 6-month durability bar — 39% of patients hit a clinically meaningful response after two doses, an effect that held for an average of six months, with launch-readiness on track for year-end.
Curaleaf's $1.5B cross-border bid signals MSO confidence — its takeover offer for Canada's Aurora Cannabis at a 45% premium marks a rare U.S.-Canada consolidation play.
Vireo-Planet 13 merger builds a 265-store MSO across 15 states — the all-stock deal positions the combined company among the largest U.S. dispensary networks by store count.

DEA rescheduling review keeps advancing despite state frustrations — California's top cannabis regulator says the agency has offered no guidance to states even as it seeks more data, a sign the Schedule III process is still very much alive.
